title: Foundational Principles of Game Design & Systemic Continuums

core_principles: Mechanics represent the granular rules, data structures, and algorithms (e.g., base speed, inventory caps, commodity exchange ratios).
Dynamics describe how mechanics interact when set in motion by player input and systemic loops (e.g., grain shortages spiking bread prices and triggering martial curfew patrol AI).
Aesthetics denote the desirable emotional and sensory responses evoked in the player (e.g., tension, claustrophobia, relief, curiosity).
exemplar_case_studies: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
modules.operational_rule: Every proposed feature RFC must explicitly specify its intended dynamic interaction and emotional aesthetic target.

core_principles: Kinetic responsiveness requires instant input acknowledgment: visual particles, audio cues, and mesh facing on frame 1 of input.
Motion parallax is essential for 3D orientation: high-contrast floor seams, vertical props, and camera spring damping create depth perception.
Input leniency (coyote time, input buffering) prevents dropped interactions at boundaries.
modules.operational_rule: The player model must visibly stride, bank, and emit floor contact feedback within 16ms of input.

core_principles: Economies must avoid arbitrary spawn tables; production must follow a Leontief input-output matrix (Raw Resource -> Refined Material -> Finished Consumable).
Every currency or commodity requires balancing sinks and faucets to prevent runaway hyperinflation.
Resource shortages must cascade into environmental, lighting, and NPC hostility changes.
modules.operational_rule: Minting a new consumable requires defining its raw production source and consumption sink.
